layers.title: Adaptive attacker-defender value
layers.summary: Prioritize defenses against the cheapest causal false-certification routes using adaptive attacker/defender reasoning rather than static checklist counts.

layers.title: Lifetime risk
layers.summary: Per-run risk can accumulate over repeated use; reusable-system assurance must account for lifetime exposure and dependence when material.

layers.title: Model-risk closure
layers.summary: Risk and quality models are assumption-bearing; preserve model-family uncertainty, misspecification challenges and decision robustness rather than treating one fitted model as truth.

layers.title: Observability
layers.summary: Every material failure must have an observation path with adequate coverage; an unobservable control trigger cannot protect certification.

layers.title: Detection-to-enforcement
layers.summary: Detected invalid states must actually block, reopen, route or remediate; dashboards and warnings alone have no certification authority.

layers.title: Crash-consistent issuance
layers.summary: Artifact identity, evidence snapshot and certificate issuance must not split across a crash or partial commit.

layers.title: Rollback resistance
layers.summary: Stale favorable state cannot overwrite newer invalidating evidence; use epoch, version and freshness binding.

layers.title: Trusted time/randomness
layers.summary: When freshness or hidden-challenge unpredictability is load-bearing, bind trustworthy time and randomness semantics.

layers.title: Software realization/reproducible builds
layers.summary: Correct assurance theory can be invalidated by implementation; bind implementation/source versions, deterministic replay and reproducible build evidence where material.

layers.title: Platform attestation
layers.summary: Require platform-execution identity only when platform substitution is a material false-certification route.

layers.title: Assurance regress
layers.summary: Do not recurse assurance forever; terminate in explicit PROVED, ASSURED or ASSUMED leaves, use conditional assurance, and keep ordinary professional work at lightweight P0/P1 unless deeper assurance is triggered.

layers.title: Latent criterion discovery
layers.summary: Treat the rubric as a hypothesis; use holistic residual, independent criterion discovery and promotion tests to find decision-relevant missing dimensions without pretending universal criterion completeness.

layers.title: Residual attribution
layers.summary: Residual quality can arise from nonlinearity, interactions, context, measurement, evaluator noise or latent criteria; discriminate among explanations before adding constructs.

layers.title: Stakeholder aggregation
layers.summary: Separate epistemic judgment from normative authority; preserve user requirements, audience needs, professional convention and reviewer taste, using Pareto/necessary dominance/minimax regret instead of unjustified averaging.

layers.title: Surrogate validity/target anchoring
layers.summary: AI-judge reliability is not target-professional validity; calibrate near finalists and target populations with professional/outcome grounding, local bias estimates and OOD boundaries.

layers.title: Adaptive Goodhart
layers.summary: Evaluator validity can collapse under optimizer pressure; track search pressure, attack the surrogate, preserve exploit archives, freeze dev evaluators and use fresh generator-blind terminal evidence.

layers.title: Evidence ancestry
layers.summary: Model/provider/prompt/rubric/reference/data ancestry can create common error; independence requires genealogical and empirical error diversity, not different labels alone.

layers.title: Selection noise/optimizer's curse
layers.summary: Large noisy search selects lucky errors; search evidence is not certification evidence, so use fresh finalist evaluation and track regret, ties and winner-identity uncertainty.

layers.title: Evaluation resolution
layers.summary: Define meaningful difference and evaluator resolution; use comparison intervals, practical equivalence and abstention, and qualify near the actual decision boundary.

layers.title: Absolute quality floor
layers.summary: Relative best does not imply professional excellence; maintain criterion-referenced floors, vetoes, outcome requirements and explicit states for below-standard, standard-met-search-open and excellent-search-closed.

layers.title: Anchor/provenance contamination
layers.summary: Prestige, brand or provenance can bias judgment; use blind intrinsic channels, provenance swaps, candidate-blind standard setting and never let Opus provenance itself define excellence.

layers.title: Anchor memorization/training contamination
layers.summary: Public anchors may be recognized despite blinding; use private shadow anchors, twins, transformed controls and fresh post-freeze examples, and never treat exposure as generalization evidence.

layers.title: Challenge-generation validity
layers.summary: Fresh challenge is insufficient; require freshness, construct validity, diagnostic value, representativeness and oracle soundness, with generator and oracle separated.

layers.title: Challenge-to-deployment transport
layers.summary: Test distributions need not match deployment; separate representative, stress and mechanism suites, require support before reweighting, and bind claim tiers to demonstrated transport envelope.

layers.title: Performative deployment
layers.summary: Deployment policy can alter future populations and evidence; separate exogenous from endogenous shift, retain external anchors, account for selection and watch for self-confirming loops or diversity collapse.
